title: Version compatibility grid and staged rollout policy for channels
creator: Ava Chen
description: Consolidate a single compatibility grid and a staged rollout policy that spans the runtime, public API, official SDKs, and Console. This ticket captures the proposed channel definitions, versioning guarantees, backport windows, and the upgrade automation required for safe LTS rollouts.
context: We currently have ad-hoc compatibility notes across runtime PRDs, API docs, and SDK repos. Customers and platform teams are asking for an explicit, machine-readable policy that the Console and SDKs can reference to determine safe upgrades and pinning behavior for Dedicated/Private clusters.
goals: Define canonical channels (LTS, Stable, Edge) and lifespan guarantees for each surface
Produce a single compatibility grid mapping runtime releases to API versions, SDK semver ranges, and Console feature compatibility
Specify rollout gates and telemetry-based rollback triggers for automated orchestrations
Design a minimal upgrade-tooling surface (CLI + webhook) to perform canary updates, preflight checks, and forced rollbacks
scope: Public HTTP API versioning policy and deprecation windows
Official SDK compatibility ranges and allowed breaking change process
Console migration flags and UI compatibility for pinned customers
Automation playbook for canary -> ramp -> full rollout
out_of_scope: Third-party community SDKs (these will be encouraged but not enforced)
Billing and quotas policy changes unrelated to API versioning
Large-scale data migrations for customer model artifacts (handled in separate project)
constraints: Runtime major version bumps may require coordinated SDK patch releases for ABI shims
Private deployments have staggered upgrade windows and may not accept automatic upgrades
Console UX must avoid breaking existing dashboards for pinned customers during LTS patches
proposed_policy: Channels: Edge (rolling, immediate), Stable (minor/patch releases, supported 6 months), LTS (major baseline, support window 18 months + 12 months security-only)
Versioning: SemVer for SDKs and runtime; API uses explicit version in Accept-Version header and a stable v1/v2 mapping for backwards incompatible changes
Compatibility guarantees: patches preserve public contract; minors add non-breaking features; majors may introduce breaking changes but must provide migration notes and SDK shims where feasible
Deprecation windows: announce 90 days before breaking deprecation for Stable, 180 days for LTS major migrations
compatibility_matrix: Channel | Runtime | Public API | SDKs (JS/Python/Go) | Console
LTS-2025 | runtime-2.0.x | api-v1 (stable) | sdk-js 1.x, sdk-py 1.x, sdk-go 1.x (patch-only) | console-2025.2 (compatible, feature flags for new UI)
Stable | runtime-2.1.x (minors) | api-v1+nonbreaking v2-features | sdk latest (minor+patch support) | console-latest (recommended)
Edge | runtime-main (nightly/fast) | api-experimental (opt-in) | sdk-canary (opt-in) | console-canary (developer opt-in)
Notes: SDKs will publish 'compatibility.json' in release artifacts that maps supported runtime and API versions for automation consumers
rollout_gates: Preflight: unit/integration test matrix against targeted runtime+api combination
Canary: 1% traffic on hosted API, single Dedicated pool for private customers that opt-in
Telemetry gate: token-level latency P50 increase <= 10% and error rate <= 0.2% over baseline
Artifact gate: successful end-to-end SDK regressions for JS/Python/Go
Manual approval: required for LTS-major transitions with >1 breaking change
upgrade_tooling: Preflight suite runner that executes smoke tests, schema checks, and customer-config linting
Webhook-based rollout orchestrator for Dedicated/Private that respects customer maintenance windows
A small compatibility service that serves compatibility.json for each release and a plain JSON compatibility grid endpoint
automation_playbook: Step 0: dry-run, produce compatibility report and list of impacted SDK pins
Step 1: push runtime artifact to staging; run full preflight matrix
Step 2: deploy canary percentage and monitor telemetry for 4 hours
Step 3: if gates pass, ramp to 25% for 6 hours; final verification on cost & latency SLOs
Step 4: full rollout to hosted API; for Dedicated/Private, schedule upgrades per customer window and publish opt-in channel
Rollback triggers: sustained latency regression > 20% or error spike > 0.5% for 30 minutes
risk_mitigation: Keep LTS branches open for critical patches and backports; maintain a dedicated 'lts-patch' team rotation
Require automated migration tests for SDKs prior to LTS major acceptance
Provide clear pinning instructions and a migration doc per breaking change
Communicate with top 50 Dedicated customers before any LTS-major changes and offer migration assistance
acceptance_criteria: Single canonical compatibility grid published in Confluence and a machine-readable endpoint
redwoodctl implements preview and apply flows and passes integration tests in CI
Rollout playbook validated in a non-production staging environment with a mock Dedicated cluster
Sign-off from Product (Priya Nair), SDK owners (Liam O'Connor), and Security (Jordan Patel)
